detail:
Mayo Clinic notes that some people with essential tremor do not require treatment when symptoms are mild, and that treatment is considered when tremor makes work or daily activities difficult. Diagnosis involves a review of medical and family history and a physical and neurological examination; there are no medical tests that diagnose essential tremor directly, so clinicians may run blood and urine tests or, in uncertain cases, a dopamine transporter scan to rule out other conditions such as Parkinson's disease.

Medicine classes Mayo Clinic describes include beta blockers, anti-seizure medicines, tranquilizers, and nerve-blocking botulinum toxin injections, which the source notes may be useful for head and voice tremors. Physical and occupational therapy, weighted utensils and other adaptive tools, and a wearable peripheral nerve stimulation device are also described. For severely disabling tremor that does not respond to medicines, Mayo Clinic describes surgical options including deep brain stimulation, in which an electrode is placed in the thalamus, and focused ultrasound thalamotomy, a noninvasive procedure that uses focused sound waves.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about managing essential tremor and its treatments.
summary: Mayo Clinic describes essential tremor care that ranges from no treatment for mild symptoms to beta blockers and other medicine classes, therapy and adaptive tools, and deep brain stimulation or focused ultrasound for severe, disabling tremor.
takeaways: mild tremor may need no treatment, the source notes
medicine classes include beta blockers and anti-seizure medicines
never start, stop, or change medicines without your doctor
title: Essential Tremor: treatment options from medicines to focused ultrasound
